name: AWS 3-Tier Architecture
statusNote: Learning project built step by step in the AWS console. No Terraform (per its README).
summary: A secure three-tier network on AWS: an Application Load Balancer for users, OpenVPN as the only admin path to SSH, and a Squid proxy as the controlled way out for private servers.

caseStudy.problem: Application servers should not be reachable from the internet, admins still need SSH, and private servers still need packages. Each path needs its own, narrow door.
approach: One VPC with four subnets, an internet gateway, and separate public and private route tables in ap-south-1.
Users reach the frontend and backend only through the ALB, with path routing for /api/*.
Admins connect through OpenVPN, locked to their own IP, before SSH. Private hosts reach the internet only through Squid.

architecture.caption: Three doors: ALB for users, OpenVPN for admins, Squid for egress.

nodes.label: Admin (MyIP)
nodes.note: The VPN security group allows only the admin's public IP.

nodes.label: ALB :80
nodes.note: APP security group. Target groups for frontend and /api/* backend.

nodes.label: OpenVPN :1194
nodes.note: Public host with an Elastic IP; the only way to reach SSH.

nodes.label: Frontend :80
nodes.note: Private subnet, no public IP. Web security group.

nodes.label: Backend :8000
nodes.note: Private subnet, no public IP. /api/health returns ok.

nodes.label: SSH :22
nodes.note: Connect security group allows SSH only from the VPN.

nodes.label: Squid :8888
nodes.note: Proxy security group. Private hosts send outbound traffic here.

nodes.label: Internet
nodes.note: Package repositories, reached only through the proxy.

decisions: One security group per role (APP, Web, Backend, Proxy, Remote, VPN, Connect) keeps every rule narrow and readable.
No public IPs on application servers.
A documented cleanup order (ALB, target groups, instances, EIP, security groups, subnets, VPC) because the ALB is billed.
security: SSH is reachable only through the VPN, and the VPN only from the admin's IP.
Private servers have controlled egress through a proxy instead of a NAT to everything.
deployment: Built from a master checklist and a step-by-step DEPLOY.md, with boot scripts in userdata/.
Tested by checking the ALB DNS, /api/health, healthy target groups, VPN-to-SSH and the proxy path.
limitations: Manual console build; no infrastructure as code yet.
